correctness.rationale: The quartic and base field are fixed explicitly. Direct differentiation proves the sole projective singular-support point, and Veniani (arXiv:1606.02135, Section 6) identifies its A3 type and the sharp global bound of 68 geometric lines (Theorem 1.1). A complete 68-row Grassmannian certificate over F64, encoded using an irreducible degree-six polynomial, passes five binary-quartic coefficient identities at every row. The independent six-chart C++ enumeration exhausts all 17,047,617 F64 lines and matches those 68 rows exactly. The geometric upper bound proves there are no additional lines over an algebraic closure. Frobenius squaring closes the row set and has exact orbit counts four, two, two and nine orbits of lengths one, two, three and six. At each row the local Grassmannian defining Jacobian has full column rank; with the finite geometric support this proves the scheme reduced and hence finite etale. The plane factorization gives the two rational and one conjugate-pair cuspidal cycles, and the rational-point and zeta formulas follow by the standard orbit identities. All code and evidence are included.

originality.rationale: The prior geometric 68-line bound and family are credited, not newly claimed. The addition is the explicit F2 Frobenius class, all extension-field line counts and line-scheme zeta function, and reducedness at all 68 geometric points. Direct comparison with the relevant full-text geometric results, semantic mathematical-record queries and targeted bibliographic searches has not identified a statement that implies this complete arithmetic and infinitesimal classification. This is best-knowledge originality, with acknowledged residual risk from specialized unpublished and unindexed calculations.
residual_risks: A specialized finite-field database, archived code or unpublished calculation could already contain the same orbit numbers.

value.rationale: This is an extreme and geometrically distinguished 68-line quartic family unique to characteristic two. Knowing the full arithmetic splitting and reduced line-scheme structure is a natural refinement of its geometric maximum, with exact consequences over every field extension. The minimal splitting degree six and distinction between the four cuspidal plane lines and 64 special lines have intrinsic mathematical motivation. The full tangent calculation prevents conflation of the 68 geometric support points with a possibly nonreduced Hilbert scheme. The result is neither an arbitrary parameter slice (the binary ground field has a unique nonzero parameter) nor a routine substitution into a preexisting Frobenius table.
